subject: general
question: Two objects of different masses are dropped from the same height in vacuum. Which one will reach first?

options.text: Both reach the ground at the same time.
Both reach at different times, depending on shape and size.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both reach the ground at the same time**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In a **vacuum**, there is a total absence of **air resistance** or **atmospheric pressure**. This means that no external force other than **gravity** acts upon the objects as they fall.
 
• According to the principles of **classical mechanics**, the **acceleration due to gravity** (denoted as **g**) is constant for all objects near the surface of the **Earth**, regardless of their **mass**, **volume**, or **density**.
 
• The **time of flight** for an object in **free fall** from a height **h** is given by the kinematic equation **t = square root of (2h/g)**. Because the variable for **mass** (m) does not appear in this formula, the time taken to reach the ground is identical for all objects. ***Hence, the correct answer is statement 2.***
 
• The observation that all bodies fall at the same rate was famously proposed by **Galileo Galilei** in the **late 16th century**, contradicting the **Aristotelian** theory which suggested that heavier objects fall faster.
 
• The value of **g** is approximately 9.8 meters per second s
